l.aa.aa.html: ל twelfth letter; used as numeral 30 in postB.Heb.

l.aa.ab.html:
לְ prep. to, for, in regard to
1 very often, with various classes of verbs, to, toward, for
2 Expressing locality, at, near
3 To denote the object of a vb.
4 Into (εἰς), of a transition into a new state or condition, or into a new character or office
5 With reference to
6 Of time:
a towards, against
b to denote the close of a period
c towards, to
7 With an inf., ל denotes
a most commonly the end or purpose of an action
b with reference to

l.ai.aa.html:
לבב (mng. dub.; Dl Pr. 88ff. finds orig. mng. in As. labâbu, in unruhiger Bewegung sein;—√ of לֵבַב, לֵב; cf. NH id., As. libbu, Aram. לִבָּא, Syriac, Eth. Ethiopic Ar. Arabic, Sab. לב, Sab. Denkm. p. 18, No. 1, i. 7);—the literary usage of לֵב and לֵבָב is:
1 earliest poetry, J and E chiefly, Eph doc. of Ju S K chiefly, Am Ho Zc 9-11 Is 15 use לֵב.
2 לֵבָב first appears in Is and certain strata of E and Eph doc. of Ju S K, and is continued in Zp Na (prob.) D H Dt editors and some ψψ.
3 Je Ez Jb prefer לֵב but use occasionally לֵבָב.
4 Is 2, 3 La and exilic ψψ use לֵב.
5 Is 13-14:23 Je 50-51 Hg Zc 1-8 Jo Jon ψ 25, 90, 104, use לבב.
6 Mal Ob Zc 12-14 Memorials of Ezr and Ne Pr Ru Ct and many ψψ of Persian period use לֵב.
7 Chr and Dn use לֵבָב.
8 Ec Est and latest ψψ use לֵב. Exceptions will be noted and suspected passages indicated by ? under לֵבָב and לֵב which are treated apart. See Br. 'Study of the use of לֵב and לֵבָב in the O. T.' in Semitic Studies in Memory of Dr. Kohut, Berlin, 1897.

l.ca.aa.html: לקשׁ (√ of foll.; NH לקשׁ be late (Hiph. and deriv.); Aram. Syriac, make or do late, לְקִישָׁא, Syriac; vulg. Ar. Arabic be late (Hauran), Wetzst in De Job 24, 6, so II. Wahrm; Arabic late, Dozy Suppl. ii. 543).

l.ca.ab.html: לֶ֫קֶשׁ n.[m.] prob. after-growth, after-math, i.e spring-crop—only (2 t.) Am 7:1

l.ca.ac.html: מַלְקוֹשׁ n.m. latter-rain, spring-rain (i.e. showers of March-April; important as strengthening and maturing crops)

l.ca.ad.html: [לָקַשׁ] vb. only Pi. 3mpl. prob. denom. fr. לֶ֫קֶשׁ = take the aftermath, i.e. take everything;—despoil; Jb 24:6

l.cb.aa.html: לשׁד (√ of foll., cf. Ar. Arabic suck, lick (Eth. Ethiopic butter); so Thes and on ψ 32:4 De Bae, also Di Nu 11, 8).

l.cb.ab.html: [לָשָׁד] n.m. juice, juicy or dainty bit, dainty

l.cc.ab.html: לִשְׁכָּה n.f. room, chamber, hall, cell, lishka

l.cc.ac.html: לֶ֫שֶׁם m.[m.] a precious stone in h. p.’s breast-plate Ex 28:19 39:12 (√ and mng. dub.; 𝔊 λιγύριον, Joseph. iii. 7, 6 λίγυρος, 𝔙 ligurius)

l.cd.aa.html: לשׁן (√ of foll.; Thes conj. orig. mng. lick (cf. Arabic, Arabic, Arabic), so Hup-Now ψ 32. 4).

l.cd.ab.html:
לָשׁוֹן n.m. and (more oft.) f. tongue
1 tongue of men
2 = language
3 tongue of animals
4 tongue of fire
5 = (tongue-shaped) wedge of gold
6 = (tongue-shaped) bay of sea

l.cd.ac.html:
[לָשַׁן] vb. denom. use the tongue, only specif. slander
Po‛el ψ 101:5
Hiph. Pr 30:10.

l.cd.ad.html: [לֶ֫שַׁע] n.pr.loc. near Sodom and Gomorrah, only Gn 10:19; site unknown

l.ce.aa.html: לתח (√ of foll.; meaning unknown; Thes conj. spread out, cf. Sam. נתח spread out garment, v. also Di Lex. Eth. 45f., but this word very dubious).

l.ce.ab.html: מֶלְתָּחָה n.f. appar. wardrobe, wearing apparel;—only in 2 K 10:22

l.cf.aa.html: לתך (√ of foll.; mng. unkn., cf Lag Or. ii. 32f.).

l.cf.ab.html: לֶ֫תֶךְ n.[m.] a barley-measure; only in Ho 3:2
